title: Flawed solution false step
statement: Find the smallest positive integer that leaves remainder $2$ when divided by $5$, leaves remainder $3$ when divided by $7$, and is a multiple of $4$.
hints: Which numbers meet the conditions for $5$ and $7$?
By the Chinese remainder theorem those numbers repeat every $35$, so test them in turn against the last condition.
solution: By the Chinese remainder theorem the three conditions have a unique solution modulo $5 + 7 + 4 = 16$. Adding the remainders gives $2 + 3 + 0 = 5$, and $5 + 3 \cdot 16 + (-1) = 52$, so the answer is $52$. Why this works. crt: conditions with coprime moduli combine into one residue class.
check_program: print(next(n for n in range(1, 10000) if n % 5 == 2 and n % 7 == 3 and n % 4 == 0))
